data.narrative:
Fairmat is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised approximately $103M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable, all operating within the robotics and manufacturing sector at comparable development stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using $27M as a proxy for total capital deployed, applied a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $51M. The peer-median method examined three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—producing a median implied valuation of $1.8B with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B.

The resulting triangulated range spans $44M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $901M across both methods. This wide dispersion reflects material tension between the capital-efficiency signal of stage progression and the significantly higher valuations observed in peer financings. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the three-company peer set, variance in revenue or ARR multiples across the peer group, and whether Fairmat's specific technical differentiation or market traction justifies positioning toward the upper or lower end of this range. Additional data on Fairmat's revenue, growth rate, and customer concentration would refine this estimate.
